transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because I feel like I’m always running hot, you know? Like I can’t shut the motor off. It’s just go, go, go. And lately, that’s been getting me in trouble at the firehouse. Which is crazy because usually, that kind of energy is great for the job. Like last week, we had this massive brush fire out on County Road 9. Huge flames, wind blowing everywhere. I was out there for twelve hours straight, didn't even stop to eat. Reminded me of this time I went camping with my brother up in the Adirondacks, and we tried to build a fire with wet wood. Took us hours, and we ended up just eating cold beans out of a can. He was so mad. Anyway, yeah, I just can't seem to turn it off, and the captain is starting to get on my case about it.
Does this high-energy, can't-shut-it-off feeling come in distinct periods, or is it pretty much always been there?
I mean, I'm not really sure if it's in periods or what. It feels like it's just... always kind of humming, you know? Like, even
Did you have this same can't-slow-down, always-on feeling when you were a child?

Yeah, my mom says I was exactly like this back in grade school, too. She always tells these stories about how I was constantly out of my seat, just blurting out answers before the teacher even finished asking the question. And I was always losing my homework. She used to get all these notes sent home from my teachers saying I was bright enough to do
Have you ever had a period where your mood felt unusually high or irritable compared with your normal self?

No, not really. I mean, my mood is just my mood. I get annoyed sometimes, sure, especially when we're doing rig checks and the guy before me didn't restock the medical bags. That drives me crazy. I mean, it's a safety issue, right? You open the bag at a scene and there's no trauma dressings. Reminds me of this time my buddy Dave and I were fixing up this old '68 Mustang. Beautiful car, cherry red. We spent all weekend pulling the engine, and when we went to put it back together, we realized we were missing like half the bolts. We had to drive to three different hardware stores just to find the right ones. Dave was so mad he almost threw a wrench through the windshield. But yeah, no, I wouldn't say my mood gets unusually high or anything. Just normal annoyed, you know?
Do you often feel worried or anxious, even when there isn’t an immediate emergency or problem to handle?

Anxious? No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really sit around worrying if there's nothing going on. I mean, obviously when the tones drop at the station, your adrenaline goes up, but that's just normal for the job. People call us for the craziest things, though. Like, last
